case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 11th day of August, 2010 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.2750 of 2009).
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 11th day of August, 2010 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 2750 of 2009 discharging the Rule.

2. The present petitioners filed the writ petition before the High Court Division impugning the order dated 05.02.2009 passed by the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj in Artha Rin Decree Execution Case No.149 of 2005 rejecting their application  under Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) filed for setting aside the auction sale held on 06.09.2006.

3. In the writ petition it was stated, inter-alia, that on 27th April, 2004 the respondent-Bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No.401 of 2004 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj for realization of. TK.13,48,765.00 initially against M/S. Shahjahan Store, represented by its proprietor Md. Shahjahan and Jahangir, sons of late Jahed and Rashida Akhter, wife of Abdul Malek. On 05.08.2004 the suit was decreed ex-parte in preliminary form. As the judgment-debtors did not pay the decretal amount to the decree-holder bank it levied Artha Rin Execution Case No.149 of 2005 for execution of the decree. The respondent-Bank concealed all the notices of the execution case and, therefore, the petitioners did not know anything about the execution case. The execution ease was fixed on 06.09.2006 for auction sale of the scheduled property and on that date the same was sold in auction   at TK. 13,50,000.00 being the highest bid. The decree-holder Bank and the executing Court accepted the bid though the execution case was levied for recovery of Tk. 15,26,614.00, The petitioners being the owners of the scheduled property filed an application before the executing Court on 26.09.2006 under Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code for setting aside the auction sale by making deposit of an amount of TK.14,17,500.00= (13,50,000.00 + 67,500.00) as statutory requirement. The executing Court rejected the application by its order dated 20.11.2006 on the finding that the application was not filed in accordance with law. In the order dated 20.11.2006 the executing Court did not mention anything about the shortfall of the required statutory amount and as a result, the petitioners could not know the real cause for rejecting the application to set aside the auction sale. The conducting lawyers did not also tell the petitioners about the mistake committed by them.

4. Being aggrieved by the order dated 20.11.2006, the petitioners filed Writ Petition No. 3326 of 2007 before the High Court Division and Rule was issued in the writ petition on 03.04.2007. At the time of issuance of the Rule, all further proceedings of the execution case were stayed. A Division Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing the writ petition by its judgment and order dated 04.01.2009, discharged the Rule on the ground that the entire money as required by law was not deposited. At the time of hearing of the writ petition for the first time it came to the notice of the petitioners that there was a shortfall of TK. 1,76,114.00, that is, in place of TK. 15,26,114+67,5000 a sum of TK. 14,17,500.00 was deposited at the time of filing the application under Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code.

5. In the writ petition it was further contended that the less amount was deposited due to the wrong advice of the lawyer. Immediately, after obtaining the certified copy of the judgment of the said writ petition on 18.01.2009 the petitioners went to the concerned Court and they were advised to make payment of the balance amount of Tk. 1,76,114.00 in addition to the deposit already made by them earlier and accordingly, on 28.01.2009 they filed an application for setting aside the auction sale on payment of balance amount and the same was fixed for hearing on 05.02.2009, but meanwhile the executing Court heard an application filed by the auction purchaser on an off-date and passed an order for placing boinama before the Sub-registrar which clearly indicates out and out malafide by the executing Court. The executing Court by the order dated 05.02.2009 rejected the application filed by the petitioners. Till 05.02.2009 the writ of possession has not been issued in the case and the petitioners are in possession of the scheduled property which they have been possessing for more than 100 years in successive generations. The approximate market value of the auction sold property would be more than 800% to the auction money.

6. The writ petition was contested by respondent Nos. 2 and 4, the decree-holder and the auction purchaser respectively by filing two separate sets of affidavit-in-opposition stating almost similar facts. In the affidavits-in-opposition the respondents contended that the executing Court correctly and rightly rejected the petitioners earlier application under Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code as they did not make the statutory deposit. Moreover, the order of the executing Court having been confirmed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3326 of 2007, there was no scope for the executing Court concerned to allow the subsequent application of the petitioners filed after more than 2(two) years from the date of the auction sale in question. The writ-petitioners most collusively and fraudulently mortgaged the scheduled property to the House Building Finance Corporation for which the auction purchaser had to pay an additional amount or TK. 4,70,000.00 to it for releasing the some but the Writ petitioners did not deposit the said money paid by the auction purchaser. The impugned order did not suffer from any legal infirmity and as such, the Rule was liable to be discharged.

7. A Division Bench of the High Court Division which heard the writ petition by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule on 3(three) grounds: (I) previously the writ-petitioners filed an application under Order XXI, rule 139 of the Code for setting aside the auction sale but the same was rejected for non-deposit of the required money as per the provision of law, (II) the earlier order of rejection of the application filed under Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code was affirmed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.3326 of 2007 against which the petitioners did not file any appeal to this Division and (III) the second application was filed after more than 2(two) years from the date of auction sale, Hence this petition for leave to appeal.

8. Mr. M. Amir-Ul Islam, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners, has contended that the judgment-debtors fulfilled their obligations by paying the entire amount of the auction sale and the interest amounting to TK. 14,17,500.00+TK. 1,85,000.00, that is, in total TK. 16,02,500.00 and also by paying in Court the dues of the House Building Finance. Corporation amounting to TK.4,70,000.00 and thus, there has been due and substantial compliance of the requirement of Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the learned Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in affirming the order passed by the executing Court on the erroneous approach that the second application with the deposit of shortfall having been filed after more than two years, the petitioners were not entitled to get the relief in law. In this regard the learned Judges failed to consider that the delay in depositing the shortfall of the statutory deposit took place due to the wrong advice of the lawyer and such fact was also not at all spelt out in the order of the executing Court. Mr. M. Amirul Islam has further contended that the decree-holder and the auction purchaser acted malafide in collusion with each other in holding the auction of the scheduled property inasmuch as in making the advertisement for sale, it was not disclosed that there is a two storied house in the scheduled property which is nothing but suppression of material fact and, that was enough to set aside the auction sale but the learned Judges of the High Court Division failed to consider these factual and legal aspects of the case and thus, erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and order. Mr. Islam has further contended that the order dated 26.09.2006 by which the petitioners first application was rejected being non-transparent and nothing having been said as to the shortfall in making the statutory deposit while filing the application and after the judgment was passed in the writ petition the petitioners deposited the same which shows their bonafide and anxiety to set aside the auction sale, the High Court Division fell into an error in not interfering with the order of the executing Court on the view that the deposit of the shortfall was made after more than 2(two) years. Mr. Islam has lastly contended that the order of the executing Court is coram-non-judice, the same having not been constituted in accordance with the provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and as such, the auction sale is liable to be set aside.

9. On the above submissions, Mr. Islam prays for granting leave by this Division.

10. Mr. M. A. Samad, learned Counsel, entering caveat on behalf of respondent No. 4, the auction purchaser, on the other hand, has contended that the High Court Division rightly discharged the Rule by the impugned judgment and order inasmuch as the petitioners application was not maintainable in law due to the non-deposit of the statutory requirement.

<u>11. From the facts as discussed, hereinabove, it appears that the petitioners first application for setting aside the auction sale held on 06.09.2006 was filed within time by making the statutory deposit to the tune of TK. 14,17,500.00, but because of miscalculation there was a shortfall of TK. 1,76,114 which they already deposited by filing application on 28.01.2009 along with the other deposit and thus, there was due and substantial compliance of the provisions of Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code after disposal of Writ Petition No.3326 of 2007, but the executing Court refused to accept the same on the view that the shortfall was deposited after long 2(two) years from the date of auction sale. Moreover, it appears that in the schedule of the property sold in auction the fact of existence of a two storied house was also omitted which is a material omission.</u>

<u>12. In view of the above, we find merit in the submissions of Mr. M. Amirul Islam and, therefore, leave is granted to consider the following points:</u>

<u>I. Whether the High Court Division was justified in affirming the order passed by the executing Court rejecting the petitioners' application to accept the shortfall of the statutory deposit amounting to TK. 1,76,114 plus the dues of the House Building Finance Corporation on the ground of delay of two years in depositing the same from the date of auction sale, though by such deposit there was due and substantial compliance of the requirement of Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the first application having been filed well within time.</u>

<u>II. Whether the decree-holder and the auction purchaser acted malafide in collusion with each other in concealing the particulars of the property sold in auction by omitting the fact of existence of a two storied house in the schedule of the property while making advertisement for selling the same in auction, a fact which is sufficient to set aside the auction sale.</u>

<u>III. Whether taking of adjournments of the hearing of the application for setting aside the auction sale by the auction purchaser and the decree holder had any impact in the delay of the disposal of the same and whether such tactics had any bearing in passing  the non-transparent order by the executing Court and, if so, can those be considered as sufficient ground for setting aside the auction sale.</u>

<u>IV. Whether the order of the executing Court is coram-non-judice, the same having not been constituted in accordance with the provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.</u>

13. Security of TK. 1000.00 is to be deposited within one month.

14. The preparation of paper books is dispensed with as prayed for.

15. The order of status-quo granted earlier shall continue till disposal of the appeal.

16. The appellant shall submit the concise statements by 12th April, 2011 and 1(one) week thereafter the respondent will file the concise statements.

End.

Mr. Borhanuddin, J :- Since both the civil revisions arises out of a single judgment and the parties are also same, these civil revisions are disposed by this common judgment. 

2. In Civil Revision No.2129 of 2009 Rule has been issued in the following terms : 
"The Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party nos.1-2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 11.05.2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Narayangonj in Title Appeal No.165 of 2007 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 08.07.2007 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Araihajar, Narayangonj in Title Suit No.174 of 2005 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper."

3. In Civil Revision No.2440 of 2009 Rule has been issued in the following terms : 
"The Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party nos.1-4(Jha) to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree complained of in the petition should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper."

4. Common facts relevant for disposal of the Rules are that the opposite party nos.1 and 2 herein as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.174 of 2005 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Araihajar, Narayangonj, for partition of ejmali property measuring an area of 1.55 acres out of 6.21 acres of the suit land contending interalia that the suit land compromising 10 Plots in C.S. khatian No.36 measuring 5.32 acres and .89 acres of land in C.S. khatian No.441 originally belonged to C.S. recorded tenant Pi Mahmud who died leaving 3 (three ) sons Bochai, All Mahmud and Choly Mahmud and 2 (two) daughters Izzatunnessa and Lazzatunnessa. Bochai was entitled 1.5525 acres land who died leaving son Kolimuddin and daughter Putul Bibi. As the heir of Bochai, Kolimuddin was entitled 1.0350 acres land and died leaving defendant nos.1-5. Putul Bibi died leaving a daughter Pokon Bibi. Pokon Bibi died leaving husband defendant no.11, 3(three) sons defendant nos.6-8, 2(two) daughters defendant nos.9/10. All Mahmud, another son of C.S. recorded tenant Pi Mahmud was entitled 1.5525 acres land in the suit land who died leaving 2(two) sons Rahimuddin and Hazi Ahizuddin, defendant no.18 and 2(two) daughters Shairun and Shanoo. Rahimuddin died leaving 3(three) sons defendant nos.12-14 and 3(three) daughters Fazilatunnessa, Ayesa and Mossamat, defendant nos.15/A. Ayesa died laving a daughter Shahnaz. Shairun, daughter of Ali Mahmud died leaving 2(two) sons defendant nos.19/20 and 3(three) daughters defendant Nos.2 1/22/23. Shanoo, another daughter of Ali Mahmud died leaving 2(two) sons, defendant Nos.24/25 and 4(four) daughters defendant nos.26-29. Cholly Mahmud, another son of Pi Mahmud was entitled 1.5525 acres land in the suit land who died leaving 2(two) sons Taizuddin and Somuruddin and 2(two) daughters Joyrun and Mozirun, defendant nos.46/47. Taizuddin died leaving 2(two) sons defendants nos.30/31 and 5(five) daughters defendant nos.32-36 died leaving wife Khodeza, defendant no.37, son Manu Mia and 2 (two) daughters Minara and Azufa, defendant nos.44/45. Manu Mia died leaving wife Suraiya Begurn, 2(two) sons, defendant Nos.39/40 and 3(three) daughters, defendant nos.41-43. Izzatunnessa, daughter of Pi Mahmud was entitled 771/2 decimals of land and died leaving 3(three) sons Abed Ali, Isab Ali and Nawab Ali. Nawab All died leaving a son Aminuddin. Abed Ali, Isob Ali and Aminuddin, grand son of Nawab Ali, sold 771/2 decimals of land by registered deed no.542 dated 20.01.1987 to the present plaintiffs. Lazzatunnessa, another daughter of Pi Mahmud, died leaving 2(two) sons Pandob All and Sanda Ali. Pandob Ali died leaving a son Latif and Sanda died leaving only son Sukur Mahmud alias Kalai Sukkur Kahmud alias Kalai. Kalai died leaving 3(three) sons, Noor Mohammad Mia, Nurul Haq Mai, Nurul Amin Mia and a daughter Nurzahan. Amongst heirs of Sukkur Mahmud Kalia, 3 (three) sons got the suit land by mutual partition. Abdul Latif Mia, Nur Mohammad Mia, Nurul Haq Mia and Nurul Amin, the heirs of Lazzatunnessa sold the suit land measuring 771/2 decimals land on 08.02.1989 by the registered deed no.1163 to the present plaintiffs. Thus the plaintiffs acquired title in 1.55 acres of land from the suit land and possessed peacefully and uninterruptedly by mutating their names in the khatians and paying rents to the Government exchequer. Defendant nos.1-47 are the owners by way of inheritance and defendant no.55 is the owner by purchase. The plaintiffs and defendants have been occupying the suit land jointly. The plaintiffs demanded partition by metes and bounds and on 29.09.1995 the defendants denied to do so. Hence, the present suit. 

5. The defendant no.3 contested the suit by filing written statement contending interalia that the land originally belonged to Pi Mahmud who died leaving Ali, Salimuddin and Bochai. Bochai died leaving a son Kolimuddin. The C.S. record was prepared in the name of Ali, Salimuddin and Kalimuddin. Salimuddin died leaving 5(five) sons Aichally, Nazimuddin, Kasem Ali, Sawkat All and the defendant Azimuddin. Each son got .415 decimals land. Salimuddin died leaving 2(two) sons Sameruddin and Taizuddin and 2(two) daughters, each'son got .69 decimals of land and each daughter got .341/2 decimals land. Sameruddin and Mozirunnesa sold .19 decimals land from Plot no.117 on 15.05.1985 by registered deed no.1762 to this defendant and since then this defendant is in possession of the lands by constructing house and planting trees thereon. Thus, this defendant got .605 decimals land by inheritance and purchase. Pi Mahmud had no daughters namely Izzatunnessa and Lozzatunnessa. This defendant filed a declaratory suit on 27.12.1986 being Title Suit No.61 of 1985 which was decreed on contest and the father of the present plaintiffs filed appeal which was dismissed. 

6. Opposite party nos.4(ka)-(jha) being heirs of defendant no.56 contested the suit by filling written statement contending interalia that the suit land originally belonged 'to Zeminder Gokul Chandra. In the year 1925, Gokul Chandra relinquished .44 decimals land from Plot no.1055 and transferred the same to Newaz Ali Khan, father of the defendant. Since then he was occupying the lands by cultivating crops. Gokul Chandra filed a suit in the 4th Munsil Court, Dhaka and collected rents from Newaz Ali Khan for the land of Plot no.1055. Newaz Ali Khan died leaving the present defendants Mannaf Kha, Hannan Kha, Bareq Kha and a daughter Nurunessa. Later on, the land of Plot no.1055 recorded in the R.S. Khatian No.23 as R.S. Plot no.2206 in the names of defendants. Nurunnessa on 16.03.1979 by registered Ewaz deed no.835 transferred her portion to the defendants. Thus the defendants got .44 decimal land in Plot no.1055 and occupying the same peacefully and uninterrupted for more than 12 years by cultivating crops. The certified copy of Ewaz deed no.835 has been lost. The plaintiffs have no title, interest or possession in the suit land and they are not entitled to get any relief as prayed for. If the plaintiffs get decree, the defendants prayed for separate Saham for .44 decimals land in the suit Plot no.1055. 

7. Plaintiffs adduced 6(six) witnesses, defendant no.56 adduced 4(four) witnesses, defendant no.3 adduced 2(two) witnesses and defendant no.12 adduced 2(two) witnesses to prove their cases. 

8. Upon hearing the parties. The learned Senior Assistant Judge dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 08.07.2007. 

9. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs as appellants preferred Title Appeal No.165 of 2007 in the Court of learned District Judge, Narayangonj. On transferred the same was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st   Court, Narayangonj who after hearing the parties allowed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 11.05.2009 by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Araihajar, Narayangonj. 
10. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree, the heirs of the defendant No.56 as petitioners preferred Civil Revision No.2129 of 2009 and the defendant No.3 as petitioner preferred Civil Revision no.2440 of 2009 before this Court. 

11. Mr. M.A. Quddus Sheikh and Mr. Mehedi Hasan Chowdhury, learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners in Civil Revision No.2129 of 2009 by filing a supplementary affidavit sworn on 26.04.2012 submits that they were ousted by the plaintiffs from .44 decimals of land in Plot no.1055 on 04.06.2009. He also submits that the plaintiffs have no locus-standi to file a suit for partition and as such the judgment and decree are liable to be set aside. He also submits that the appellate court below failed to appreciate the evidence wherein all the P.Ws deposed in their cross-examination that they are not aware of Lazzatunnessa and Izzatunnessa, alleged daughters of Pi Mahmud and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the appellate court below failed to consider the deposition of D.W.2 Hasina Begum and Exhibits 'Ka' and `Ka(1)' by which it is proved that Pi Mahmud had no daughters in the name of Izzatunnessa and Lazzatunnessa and as such the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. He submits that the appellate court below failed to advert the findings of the trial court and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. 

12. Mr. Soeb Khan with Mr. A.M. Aminul Islam, learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner in Civil Revision No.2440 of 2009 submits that the names of Izzatunnessa and Lazzatunnessa were not recorded in C.S., S.A. and R.S. Khatians and without considering this legal aspect the appellate court below committed an error of law which occasioned failure of justice. He also submits that in a suit for partition when the plaintiffs claimed share as successor in interest of the owner of the partiable property the onus is on him to prove his assertion. He further submits that the photo state copies which are copies made from the original by mechanical process are admissible in the evidence. In support of his submissions the learned Advocate referred to the case of Akrab Ali and others -vs-Zahiruddin Kari and others reported in 30 DLR (SC) 81the case of Mahjak Shipping Co. Ltd. -vs- M.V. Sagar at present berthed at Chittagong Port and others reported in 39 DLR 425 and the case of Sree Gopal Chandra Mondal and another -vs- Lasman Dasi and others reported in 39 DLR(AD) 73. 
13. In both the civil revisions Md. Deiwar Hossain with Mrs. Salma Begum, learned Advocates appearing for the opposite party nos.l-2. Mr. Deiwar Hossain submits that though the named of Izzatunnessa and Lazzatunnessa were not appeared in the record of rights but P.W.6 and other P.Ws. as well as D.W.7 proved that Pi Mahmud had 3 (three) sons and 2(two) daughters. In this regard he submits record of right is not a document of title and it does not create or extinguish title to land. He also submits that D.W.2 Hasina Begum produced Photostat copy of Exhibits -Ka' and `Ka(1)' which are secondary evidence and she failed to explain where the originals are. He further submits that the appellate court below after independent assessment of the evidence on record passed the impugned judgment and decree and the High Court as a revisional court had hardly any jurisdiction to set aside the findings of fact by the appellate court below without discussing any fault in the factual finding by the said court. In support of his submissions, the learned Advocate referred to the case of Lal Meah being dead his heirs Momena Khatun and ors. vs. Haji Md. Ibrahim Meah and others reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61, the case of Soya Rani Guha alias Soya Rani Gupta vs. Abdul Awal Mia and others reported in 47 DLR (AD) 45 and the case of Kochi Mia @ KoChi Mia vs. Suruj Mia being dead his heirs Md. Fazlur Rahman and others reported in 51 DLR (AD) 57. 

14. Heard the Learned Advocates. Perused the revisional application, judgment of the courts below and the materials available in the tower court record. 

15. It appears that the trial court dismissed the suit on the ground that the names of Izzatunnessa and Lazzatunnessa were not recorded in C.S., S.A. or R.S. Khatian and in view of the report submitted by the U.P. Member Hasina Begum. On the other hand the appellate court below allowed the appeal on the ground that all the P.Ws deposed Pi Mahmud had 3(three) sons and 2(daughters) namely Izzatunnessa and Lazzatunnessa; certificate issued by the local Chairman proved Pi Mahmud had 3(three) sons and 2(daughters); U.P. member Hasina Begum produced Exhibit-`Ka' and `Ka-1' which are Photostat copies, no explanation regarding original was offered. After thorough discussions the appellate court below arrived at a finding that though the names of Izzatunnessa and Lazzatunnessa were not recorded in the Khatians but as their existence was proved they are co-sharer by inheritance in the suit property. 

16. The moot question is to be answered whether Izzatunnessa and Lazzatunnessa were the daughters of Pi Mahmud. All the P.Ws categorically deposed that Pi Mahmtid had 3(three) sons and 2(daughters), even D.W.7 i.e. defendant no.12 Habibur Rahman, stated in his cross-examination : “লজ্জাতুন্নেছা ইজ্জাতুন্নেছা ছিল শুনিয়াছি” certificate issued by the local Chairman i.e. Exhibits 7 amply proves that Pi Mahmud had 3 (three) sons and 2(daughters). Though U.P. Member Hasina Begum as D.W.2 identified her signature in Exhibits-1{a- I which is a Photostat copy, the writing in Exhibits, Ka' is also Photostat copy. No explanation regarding original was offered by D.W.2. It is true that the names of Izzatunnessa and 'Lazzatunnessa were not recorded in C.S., S.A. and R.S. Khatians but from the oral evidence as well as documentary evidence it is evident that Pi Mahmud had 3(three) sons and 2(daughters). In the case of Lal Meah being dead his heirs Momena Khatun and others -vs- Haji Md. Ibrahim Meah and others reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61, our apex court held : 
"Record of right is not a document of title. It does not create or extinguish title to land. At best, along with other evidence, it may support an evidence of title. By itself, it is not an evidence of title". 

17. Furthermore, the plaintiffs have been able to prove sale deed No.542 dated 20.01.1987 and deed no.1163 dated 08.02.1987. By dint of the deeds the plaintiffs mutated their names in the Khatians and paid rents to the Government exchequer. The plaintiffs produced the deeds, mutated khatian and rent receipts which are marked as Exhibit-3 series. This document amply proves that the plaintiffs are in possession of the land they are claiming. Though the defendant nos.3 and 56 claimed that no title had been passed by the aforesaid deeds but none of them challenged the deeds in a competent court of law. Advocate Commissioner Report, Exhibit-6, also proves possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land. 

18. Total area of the suit land is 6.21 acres out of which the plaintiffs are claming 1.55 acres and the defendant no.3 claims .60 1/2 decimals and defendant no.56 claim .44 decimals of land. Mr. M.A. Quddus. Sheikh by filling supplementary affidavit stated that A the defendant no.56 is ousted from his .44 decimals of land in Suit Plot No.1055 by the plaintiffs on 04.06.2009 but record shows that the instant rule was issued on 21.06.2009. In this long period of time the defendant no.56 did not take any step for recovery of the land which also proved the possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land. 

19. Trial Court relied upon the deposition of D.W.2 to prove that Pi Mahmud had no daughters. The D.W.2 U.P Member Hasina Begum produced Ext.-`Ka', application for heir certificate and identified her signature therein as Exhibit-`Ka-1'. Both Exhibits-'Ka' and `Ka-1' are Photostat copies. The writing therein are also Photostat copies. No explanation was offered regarding original copy of the Exhibit 'Ka' and `Ka-1'. The appellate court below after thorough discussions arrived at a finding : 
“এখানে লক্ষনীয় যে, হাছিনা বেগম ইউপি মেম্বার তদন্ত করিয়া রিপোর্ট দাখিল করিবেন ইহাই নিয়ম। কিন্তু দরখাস্তের ফটোকপির পর যে লেখা আছে তাহা ও ফটোকপি এবং হাছিনা বেগমের রিপোর্ট প্রদান না করিয়া উক্ত দরখাস্তের উপর লিখা বিধি-বিধান বর্হিভূত এবং সন্দেহের অবকাশ থাকিয়া যায়।”

In the case of Soya Rani Guha alias Sova Rani Gupta vs. Abdul Awal Mia and others reported in 47 DLR (AD) 45 our apex court held : 
"A party producing secondary evidence of a document is not relieved of the duty of providing the execution of the original. Even where a document is exhibited without objection the Court is to be satisfied as to its execution." 
After perusing the exhibit 'Ka' and 'Ka-(1)' the appellate court below arrived at a finding that those exhibits arouses suspicion to its genuinity. It is now settled position. of law when the court below gives decision on the basis of documents and evidence that is a question of fact and this court ordinarily should not interfere with the question of fact arrived at by a court unless it appears that the court below patently committed illegality and took a wrong view of law. 
In the case of Akrab Ali and others -vs-Zahiruddin Kari and others reported in 30 DLR(SC) 81, our apex court held : 
"In the absence of any error of law or error of procedure affecting the merits of the case the High Court Division is bound by any finding of fact, however erroneous it may appear to the High Court Division in respect of the appreciation of the evidence on which the said finding is based." 
Under the facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated above in view of the cited decisions, I am of the opinion that the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Narayangonj has not committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree dated 11.5.2009 in Title Appeal No.165 of 2007 and there is nothing to interfere with the same. 

20. In the result, both the Rules are discharged without any order as to costs. 

21. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the rules are hereby vacated.

22. Send down the lower court record. 

End.

Mr. A.M. Mahmudur Rahman, J: In this Rule the question falls for determination is whether the impugned order dated 31.7.90 directing the petitioners to publish the result of B.A. (Hon's) examination of the opposite-party 1 held in 1978 should not be set aside. This case has got a chequered career. The opposite party 1 appeared in B.A. (Hon's) examination for the year 1976 held in 1978 from Comilla Victoria College. After publication of the result he found that he failed. He challenged the result in Title Suit No. 745 of 1979 in the Court of Munsif. 3rd Court, Comilla and sought for declaration that he passed the examination and the result declared by the University of Chittagong was illegal and not binding on him. The suit was resisted by the petitioners by filing written statement. The trial court by its judgment dated August. 30, 1983 decreed the suit holding that the result of B.A. (Hon's) Examination of 1976 of the opposite-party 1 held in the month of June. 1978 was illegal and the defendant-petitioners 1-2 including another were directed to arrange publication of the result of the plaintiff afresh on computation of the average mark of the marks obtained by the opposite party 1 in all papers except the tutorial papers adding the average mark as mark obtained in the tutorial papers to total mark obtained by him in all other papers.

2. Against that decree the petitioners appeal to the learned District Judge was dismissed for default followed by an application under Or. 41 R/19 C.P.C. for re-admission of the appeal accompanied by an application for condonation of delay in filing the appeal and Miscellaneous case No. 46 of 1984 was stated. The opposite party filed an application for rejection of the Miscellaneous Case on the ground of limitation. The appellate Court dismissed the Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1984 and the order of dismissal was followed by Miscellaneous Case No. 83 of 1986 for review of the said order unsuccessfully. Thereafter the petitioners filed Civil Revision No. 142 of 1987 in the High Court Division again unsuccessfully. Thereafter the opposite party 1 filed an application under Or. 89, R 2.(3) read with S. 151 C.P.C. for guilty of negligence and for contempt of court for showing dishonour to the order of the court in not publishing the result within 30 days as directed by the trial court. The petitioners resisted that application by filing written statement stating that the average mark computed was added to the total marks obtained by the opposite party 1 and the average marks worked out was 21 and that Was the mark given in tutorial and 16 marks in viva voce examination which the opposite-party 1 already got and he even so adding the mark was declared failed and this result was communicated to him by registered post on September 16, 1989 it was further stated that the delay was unintentional in publishing the result afresh and there was no laches and negligence on their part and no dishonor was shown to the order of the court and prayed for unconditional apology. The learned Assistant Judge, however, converted the said application suo mote into an application under Or. 21 R. 32 and started Execution Case No. 19 of 1989 and on contest passed the impugned order.

<u>3. Mr. Omar Faruque appearing for the petitioners submits that the impugned order is misconceived in that it does not fall within the ambit of Or. 21 R 32 C.P.C. Or. 21 R .32 C.P.C. provides that where a party against whom a decree for Specific Performance of Contract or for restitution of conjugal rights or for an injunction has been passed and he wilfully failed to obey the order the decree may be enforced by restitution of conjugal life and in the case of Specific Performance of Contract or injunction by detention in civil prison or by attachment of his property or by both. Now the question is whether the order passed in the suit for publication of result as directed by the trial court partakes the nature of a mandatory injunction and if so whether the petitioners for wilful disobeying the same are liable for the detention in civil imprisonment or their properties are liable for attachment within the meaning of Or. 21 R. 32 C.P.C. Where on evidence it is proved that the petitioners wilfully disobeyed the order of the court in my opinion, they are liable for civil imprisonment or attachment of the property of the university on the strength of Sub-rule (2) of R. 32 of Or. 21 C.P.C. Thereafter, the contention of Mr. Omar Faruque does not appeal me though the order was passed in suit for declaration that the publication of result of an examination by the university is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff.</u>

<u>4. Let us now proceed to examine whether in the facts and circumstances of the case this court sitting in revisional jurisdiction can exercise its power under Section 151 (1) C.P.C. for securing the end of justice. Although the trial court directed to arrive at an average mark on the basis of the marks obtained in 8 general papers it appears that in general papers the opposite party 1 obtained 322 and the average of the same came to 40.25. Out of this 40.25 he was given 21 mark for the tutorial papers (Full mark for tutorial is 50) but other half of 40.25 was not given to him for viva voce. Mr. Faruque argued that as the opposite party 1 already obtained 16 marks in viva voce he was not given other half of 40.25 in viva voce in place of 16 marks obtained by him. In support of the publication of the result afresh he submits that there was no violation of the order of the court in publishing the result afresh in as much as that was done in compliance with the order of the trial court. Mr. Faruque further argued that the opposite party No. 1 is entitled only 50% of 40.25 as that was the average of the 8 papers and the total marks in tutorial was 50. Therefore, 21 marked was added to the total marks as directed by the court but still then he got plucked. The plaintiff suit rests on the assertion that he got plucked as the marks obtained by him in the total tutorial classes were not sent to the University before publication of the result. Had it been sent he ought to have been declared passed. It is in evidence that at best opposite party 1 in one tutorial paper obtained 49% mark, Ext. 2 (B). From careful examination to Ext. 2 (B) I find that he obtained 49% in tutorial in one paper. I think that instead of the aver-age mark obtained in .8 general papers and adding half of the same to the total marks 322 obtained in general papers is not required on the very face of evidence. Ext. 2(B). inasmuch as a candidate who successfully passed in all the subjects should not suffer for the negligence of the authority of person who was at fault not to send the tutorial mark obtained by the opposite party 1 before publication of the result to the university. It is in consonance with the wisdom and justice that a boy who got 49% marks in one tutorial paper and when it is in the evidence that authorities did not send the tutorial marks to the university before publication of the result the conduct of the university authority to play in such a fashion with the fact of the student to the deprivation of his legal right should not be encouraged for no fault of the student. Therefore, I modify the order passed by the trial court. 49% mark obtained in one tutorial paper means 24.50 marks out of total 50 marks for tutorial papers. Therefore, I direct to add this 24.50 to the total marks i.e. 322 obtained by opposite party 1.</u>

<u>5. Now, if this 24.50 is added to 16 marks obtained in viva voce it becomes more than 40% both in tutorial and viva voce and the boy gets the required marks to pass the examination as in order to pass Honours examination a student must obtain 40 marks in total in tutorial and viva voce. It appears that as the university allocated to the boy (21+ 16)=37 in total in tutorial and in viva voce he got plucked. But this calculation cannot be supported in view of Ext. 2(B) and in view of Ext. 8. Thus, I modify the order passed by the learned Assistant Judge in the above manner and I direct the University authority to publish the result of the student, the opposite party 1. in accordance with my direction as above. I am also of the opinion that in order to avoid public criticism and in future, to ensure due discharge of public by the officials of the university authority should take disciplinary action against the persons responsible for not sending the marks obtained in tutorial papers by this student to the university before publication of result of the examination as 1 do not find on record that the University has pleaded that the marks obtained by the student in tutorial papers were duly sent before publication of the result. On the other hand on record I find the fact otherwise.</u>

6. Accordingly, I discharge the Rule with the aforesaid modification of the impugned order. However, the modification based on calculation on the method adopted by me shall only govern this case and shall not be construed a general rule of calculation to be adopted in other cases.

7. The university authority is directed to publish the result afresh within 30 days from receipt of this order of this court.

End.

Mrs. Salina Masud Chowdury, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the order No. 25 dated 3.7.2002 and order No. 27 dated 3.8.2002 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Moulivibazar Sadar in Title Suit No. 292 of 2000 should not be set aside or such other or further order or orders be passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The present petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 292 of 2000 in the court of senior Assistant Judge, Mulvibazar, Sadar, against the defendant for mandatory injunction in order to demolish unauthorized construction concerning the land. 

3. The defendant No. I contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegation in the plaint. 

4. The plaintiff on 26.4.2002 filed an application before the trial court praying for holding local investigation into the suit land for determining the points as stated in the schedule of the said application but the trial court by the order dated 3.7.2002 rejected the said application. Subsequently the petitioner filed an application before the trial court to review the order dated 3.7.2002 rejecting the application praying for holding a local investigation and the 
trial court by the order dated 3.8.2002 rejected the said application. 

5. Being aggrieved by the orders dated 3.7.2002 and 3.8.2002 the present petitioner tiled on application before this court under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule. 

6. Mr. Nirmalendu Dev, the learned lawyer appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned trial court did not apply its judicial mind in rejecting the application filed for holding local investigation into the suit land and most erroneously held that two local inspections have earlier been held which according to the learned lawyer for the petitioner are absolutely different from local investigation as provided under order 26 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned lawyer further submits that the local inspection under order 39 Rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure is generally held for visual perception of the suit land. While local investigation under order 26 Rule 9 of the said code is required for the purpose of elucidating the matter in dispute and in the present suit local investigation was necessary in order to determine whether the construction works done covered or attracted any part of the disputed land or drain over suit plot No. 2075 and as such local inspections can not be substitute for local investigation or vice versa in any manner. He also submits that written statement filed by the defendant No. 1 which has been annexed as Annexure-B to this revisional application clearly shows that the defendants also made a statement there that the suit of the plaintiff will not stand without a local investigation. He also submits that the defendants having not tiled any written objection against the application for local investigation before the trial court can not now come before this court and oppose the Rule issued on the revisional application of the petitioner, and support the impugned orders passed by the trial court. In support to his contention the learned lawyer referred the decision as taken in the case of Noor Banu Versus Noor Mohammad as reported in 35 D.L.R (AD) page 183, where it was held by the Appellate Division that a party to suit after taking an exact stand in his plaint or written statement cannot so readily be allowed to depart from it on the ground that his opponent admitted the portion which was opposite to his stand. Justice and expediency cannot go together. 

7. Lastly the learned lawyer submits that the trial court has committed error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned orders which suffer from legal defects and if local investigation into the suit land is not held for proper adjudication as prayed for, the whole purpose for the suit will be frustrated and the petitioner shall be highly prejudiced.

8. Mr. Surojit Bhattacharjee, the learned lawyer appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 1 files the counter affidavit and submits that the trial court has committed no illegality in passing the impugned orders rejecting the prayers for holding local investigation. He submits that there is no need to hold any investigation as two local inspections were held earlier and that the fact whether the local investigation is needed or not is totally a discretionary matter depending on the court to decide. He also submits that the fact which is to be ascertained by local investigation as prayed for by the plaintiffs can very well be decided by taking evidence. Lastly he submits that the orders passed by the court below does not call for any interference by this court and thus the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

9. I have perused the revisional application, counter affidavit annexures and heard the learned lawyers appearing on behalf of the petitioner and the opposite party. 

10. The object of the investigation under order 26 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure is to obtain evidence which from it's peculiar nature can best be had from the spot itself. Such evidence enables the court to properly and correctly understand and assess the evidence on record. It appears that earlier two inspections were held under order 39 Rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Local investigations as it is expected would determine the disputed claim of-parties by spot visits by a survey knowing advocate. Local investigation is necessary for the purpose of elucidating the matter in dispute and in the present case the plaintiff made specific prayer for determining the tact whether the alleged unauthorized construction work has been done attracting or covering the disputed land and drain on the suit plot No. 2075. 

11. It appears that learned court below rejected the application for local investigation on the ground that earlier two local inspections were held. The position of the drain on the suit plot can only be investigated and determined through local investigation to be conducted by a survey knowing advocate. The court has a discretion, on doubt, in passing order allowing or not allowing local investigation but the exercise of discretion should be judicious and not fanciful. 

12. I am therefore of opinion that it would be just and proper if the prayer for local investigation is allowed. In the result the Rule is made absolute. The impugned orders dated 3.7.2002 and 3.8.2002 are hereby set aside. The trial court is directed to arrange for a local investigation by an advocate Commissioner having knowledge on Survey in order to determine the query raised by the petitioner in the application filed praying for local investigation. 

13. Communicate the copy of the judgment and order to the court concerned. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Syed Amirul Islam, J: As common questions of law are involved in these two reference applications and the parties are being same they were heard together and being disposed of by this judgment. 

	2. The reference application No. 24 of 1992 relates to assessment year 1982-83 and arises out of an order dated 24.9.90 passed by the Taxes Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka. Additional Bench No. 4, in I.T.A. No. 1411 of 1985-86. The reference application No. 25 of 1992 relates to the assessment year 1983-84 and arises out of an order dated 18.9.90 passed by the Taxes Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka, Additional Bench No. 4 in I.T.A. No. 431 of 1986-87 (Assessment year 1983-84). 

	In both these reference applications the common questions of law formulated by the petitioner is as follows:-

	(a) Whether on the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal was justified to uphold the disallowance of salary and allowances paid to Mrs. Nazma Kabir? 

	(b) Whether on the facts and in the circumstances of the case the Tribunal was justified in disallowing Bonus paid to the employees? 

	(c) Whether on the facts and in the circumstances of the case the Tribunal was justified on purchase of 'Compressor' as not being Revenue Expenditure? 

	(d) Whether on the facts and in the circumstances of the case the learned Tribunal was justified in confirming the disallowance of initial depreciation on the Addition of assets?

	(e) Whether on the facts and in the circumstances of the case the Tribunal was justified in affirming the allowances 'Export Rebate' as provided under section 14(4)(0(1) of Finance Ordinance, 1982? 

	(f) Whether the Commissioner of Taxes was justified in charging interest under Section 18-A? 

	In reference application No. 24 of 1992 one additional question has been framed namely-

	(g) Whether on the facts and in the circumstances of the case the Tribunal was justified in confirming and affirming the disallowance of Bank Interest on the ground that the Company advanced loan to sister concern irrespective of the fact that loan advanced was out of accumulated profit? 

	At the time of hearing the learned Advocate for the petitioner did not press question Nos. (e) and (f). 

	3. Mr. A.F.M. Ferojuddin Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the D.C.T. without disclosing the contents of the inspector's report to the petitioner wrongly relied upon that report and arrived at a finding t hat Mrs. Nazma Kabir was not a genuine employee of the assessee company and as such wrongly disallowed the entire amount of Tk. 2,64,588/- as admissible expenses and this finding of the D.C.T. was affirmed both by the A.J.C.T. and by the Tribunal and thereby the Tribunal committed an illegality in disallowing those expenses. 

	4. Mr. Md. Abdur Rahim Bhuiyan, the learned Assistant Attorney General, appearing for the respondent on the contrary submits that the D.C.T. as a matter of fact found that Mrs. Nazma Kabir, in fact was not the Manager of the assessee company and as she was so shown only to evade taxes. The learned A.A.G. further submits that it is true that the D.C.T. in arriving at a finding that Mrs. Nazma Kabir was not a genuine employee of the assesses company unilaterally relied on the inspector's report without disclosing the same to the assesses but on receipt of the assessment order the assessee came to know about the existence of the inspector's report and although they preferred an appeal against the order both to the A.J.C.T. and the Appellate Tribunal successively but never asked for a copy of the said report. Moreover, it is submitted by him that the assessee had opportunity to adduce evidence in rebuttal of the said report both before the A.J.C.T. and the Tribunal but for reasons best known to them they did not adduce any evidence to rebut the same. Thus in the facts and circumstances of the case non-disclosure of the contents of the inspector's report did not, in fact, prejudiced the assessee petitioner although technically there has been a violation of the principles of natural justice. 

	5. We have considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the respective parties on this point and also perused the impugned order, the first appellate order and the assessment order. On a perusal of the records it appears that the D.C.T. furnished certain basis for arriving at a finding that Mrs. Nazma Kabir was not a genuine employee of the assessee company. Mr. Bhuiyan extreneously argued that such a concern like the assessee which earned a profit of more than Tk. 13 lacs in the assessment year cannot be run without a manager and he submits that from the discussion of the A.J.C.T. it appears that the name of Mrs. Nazma Kabir tapped the list of the employees in the register and mere absence of signature by the manager who is the Chief Executive Officer of the assessee company cannot be a valid ground for sustaining the order of the D.C.T. both by the A.J.C.T. and the Tribunal. The question as to whether Mrs. Nazma Kabir was in fact an employee of the assesses company is essentially a question of fact. The A.J.C.T. confirmed the order of the D.C.T. taking into consideration the facts and circumstances as well as the materials on record and that finding of the A.J.C.T. was re-affirmed by the Tribunal. Since it is a question of fact which have been concurred by both the appellate forum, in our opinion there is no scope for us to interfere with such finding of fact which is based on materials. Thus we answer that the disallowances of Tk. 2,64,588/- paid to as salary and allowances to Mrs. Nazma Kabir is justified. 

	6. The next point for controversy between the parties is the payment of bonus. In the instant case the contention of the petitioner is that since ads a private concern they have paid incentive bonus to their employees as huge profits were made and this satisfied the requirements of Section 10(2)(x) of the Income Tax Act, 1922. But the D.C.T. and for that matter the A.J.C.T. and the Taxes Appellate Tribunal in flagrant violation of the provisions of law disallowed the payment of bonus on the ground that it was highly excessive. Mr. M.A. Rahim Bhuiyan. the learned A.A.G. submits that in the instant case the payment of bonus has been partly disallowed by the D.C.T. as being highly excessive and not being in conformity with the general practice in similar business and thus the D.C.T. rightly allowed two months bonus which is conformity with the general practice in this time of business and on that score the D.C.T. did not commit any illegality whatsoever. 

	7. On a perusal of the impugned order as well as the first appellate order and the assessment order it appears that the assessee in their return claimed as deduetable expenses an amount of Tk. 1.99,080/- as payment of bonus for six months. On a perusal of the records there is nothing to show that the bonus in question was paid as incentive bonus. In the Income Tax Act, 1922 (hereinafter called the Act) the bonus has not been defined in Section 4 of the Act. However, this word finds its place in Section 10 (2)(x) wherein it has been said that any sum payed to an employee as bonus or commission for services rendered, where such sum would not have been payable to him as profits or dividend if he had not been paid as bonus or commission: Provided that the amount of bonus is of a reasonable amount with reference to the pay of the employee arid the conditions of his service; the profits of the business for the year in question and the general practice in similar business. 

	It appears from a perusal of the assessment order that in the same line of business usually only two bonus are paid. Further it appears that it was found by the D.C.T. to be highly excessive. Thus, it appears that the payment of bonus made by the assessee is hit by the proviso to section 10(2)(x) of the Act. Therefore it appears that both the A.J.C.T. and the Tribunal taking a correct view of law and facts unheld the decision of the D.C.T. Therefore we are of the opinion that the payment of six months' bonus was unjustified. 

	8. The next point which calls for determination in this reference is whether the payment made by the assessee applicant for replacement of 'Compressor' of the Air Conditioner is a capital expense or the revenue expense. It is submitted by Mr. Ferojuddin Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, that in the instant case the assesses applicant spent that amount for making the unworkable Air Conditioner workable by replacing the unworkable compressor and replacement of the compressor of the Air Conditioner did not, in fact, add to the value of the assets or improved the same and thus the D.C.T. A.J.C.T. and the Tribunal all were wrong in not allowing expenses as deductible expenses treating the same as revenue expenses. The learned Assistant Attorney General tried to impress upon us that since by replacement of the compressor the assesses company will get benefit of the same which will be spread over than a year, it as rightly been treated by the D.C.T. as capital expenditure. From a perusal of the records we find it difficult to accept the submission of the learned A.A.G. All expenses generally incurred by way of repairing, replacement and renew-al of existing assets which do not in any way add to their earning capital but simply serve to maintain the original equipment is renewal expenditure. In the instant case as a matter of fact it appears that by replacing the compressor of the Air Conditioner there has not been any addition to the value of assets and as such the D.C.T. ought to have treated those as revenue expenditure and thus both the A.J.C.T. and the Tribunal erroneously affirmed the order of the D.C.T. on that score without considering this aspect of the case. Therefore our answer is that the Tribunal was not justified in the facts and circumstances of the case to disallow the amount of Tk. 58,500/- which has been spent for replacement of the compressor and the same appears to be a revenue expenditure. 

	9. The next point of contentions between the parties centres round the initial depreciation. It is asserted by Mr. Ferojuddin Bhuiyan that the micro-bus which was acquired by the assessee was for the purpose of bringing their employees to the office and dropping them to their residences after the office hours. Since it was acquired for the purpose of the business of the assessee company it ought to have been treated as capital expenditure. Therefore they ought to have allowed initial depreciation for that assets but the D.C.T. taking an erroneous view disallowed the expenditure. The Tribunal also without considering the legal aspect mechanically affirmed the order of the A.J.C.T. 

	10. Mr. Md. Abdur Rahim Bhuiyan, the learned Assistant Attorney General submits that it is covered by the rules relating to initial asset as a capital asset and covered by the rules of initial depreciation. He therefore, finds it difficult to rebut the contention of Mr. Ferojuddin Bhuiyan. In this circumstances we are of the view that the Tribunal was not justified in affirming the disallowance of initial depreciation arid the addition of the assets. 

	11. Now we come to the final controversy which centres round the payment of cost on borrowed capital. Mr. Ferojuddin Bhuiyan the learned Advocate appearing for the assessee applicant submits that there is no finding given by the D.C.T. that the assessee petitioner have no sufficient assets of their own to advance a loan to Tk. 2,50,000/- to its sister concern inasmuch as in the assessment year it earned Tk. 2,13.000/-. The learned Advocate further submits that in the absence of any finding that the assessee had no means of its own to make advance to its sister concern the disallowances of payment of proportionate interest by the assessee for the borrowed capital is illegal and in affirming the order of the D.C.T. both the learned A.J.C.T. and the Tribunal committed the same mistake which cannot be sustained in law. Mr. Abdur Rahim Bhuiyan the learned A.A.G. finds it difficult to rebut the same. On a perusal of the impugned order and the papers annexed with the petition it appears that the U.C.T. taking an erroneous view of law did not allow the entire amount of interest as deductable expenses and the Tribunal also most illegally affirmed the order of the D.C.T. as well as the order of A.J.C.T. Therefore, we are of the opinion that the Tribunal was not justified in affirming the disallowance of bank interest on the ground that the company advanced loan to the sister concern irrespective of the fact that the loan advanced was out of accumulated profit. 

	12. In view of our aforesaid discussions the questions are answered as indicated above. However, there will be no order as to cost.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Rais Uddin, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.05.2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur in Title Appeal No.51 of 1991 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 13.3.1991 passed by the learned Additional Assistant Judge, Chandpur in Title Suit No.51 of 1990 dismissed the suit, should not be set-aside.

2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that Opposite-party No.1 as plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration that kabala executed and registered by the defendants Nos.4-6 in favour of the defendant Nos.1-3 being deed No.4602 dated 14.7.1987 is illegal, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff contending, inter-alia, that predecessor of Payia Gazi who was the owner of the land under Mouza No.48 Ullaskhar, previous Khatian No.19, measuring 8.09 acres comprised under present khatian No.19. The father of the plaintiff was the original owner of the suit land along with other land having his right, title and interest over the same by way of inheritance and purchase who by way of a "will" dated 14.05.1987 transferred 2.12 1/4 acres of land in favour of the plaintiff. The defendants Nos.4-6 who are the daughters of the ancestor, had no right, title and interest but they transferred .24 acres of land by way of execution of Saf Kabala deed registered on 14.7.1987 in favour of the defendants Nos.1-3 from their ancestral land. The plaintiff declared the suit land as belonged to him by way of "Will " and prayed for declaration of the deed dated 14.7.1987 is illegal, void, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff.

3. The defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filling joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that Payia Gazi their predecessor was the original owner over the land under disputed khatian No.19 and on his death the suit land devolved upon Sree Golap Jan the wife and 5 sons, namely, Alimuddin, Karimuddin, Rahimuddin, Imamuddin and Tukka Gazi. Golap Jan died leaving her above 5 sons. Tukka Gazi being unmarried died leaving his remaining 4(four) brothers as his heirs Imamuddin their predecessor having his right, title and interest over the suit land under Khatian No.19 by way of inheritance and over the land under Khatian No.6 of Dadia Para Mouza by way of purchase, died on 1380 B.S. leaving his wife Latifa Khatun, one son and Amir Jan, Bibi Jan, Ali Jan, Korpuler Nessa, Moiyar Bhanu and Berzi Jan his daughters as his heirs and legal representative and asserted that Imamuddin never did any Will " on 14.5.1987 and as lie died in 1380 B.S. and as such execution of " Will " on 14.5.1987 is absurd not believable. These contesting defendants under the same agnate purchased .24 decimals of land as described in the written statement specifying the nature character and position of the land from the defendant Nos.4-6 the full sisters of the plaintiff by way of a registered Saf Kabala deed being deed No.4602 dated 14.7.1987 and accordingly entailed with possession over the same by the defendant Nos.4-6 who have been in possession over their respective shares. The plaintiff intending to deprive his sisters fabricated an antedated and forged deed of "Will" after 17 years of the death of his father. The plaintiff has no right, title and interest over the suit land and as such the suit of the plaintiff should be dismissed.

4. At the trial, the plaintiff examined 4(four) witnesses and defendants examined 4(four) witnesses in support of their respective cases.

5. The learned judge of the trial Court after hearing the parties, considering the evidence and materials on record dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 13.03.1991. Against the said judgment and decree the plaintiff preferred appeal before the learned District Judge, Chandpur. On transfer it was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge who after hearing the parties and considering the evidence and materials on record allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court by his judgment and decree dated 23.05.2000.

6. Feeling aggrieved, the defendants as petitioners moved this court and obtained the instant Rule.

7. Mr. Md. Amanullah with Mr. Md. Aminul Ehsan, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners has placed the revisional application, pleadings, evidence, impugned judgment and decree of the courts below before this court and submits that the plaintiff had no right to present the deed for registration of the Will " before the Sub-register as per registration Act. He submits that there was no pleading or evidence that his father instructed to present the Will for registration. He submits that the Will " is not valid will as other heirs of Imanuddin did not consent the "Will". He submits that burden lies upon the plaintiff that "Will" is genuine but the plaintiff failed to prove it. He further submits that in the pleading and evidence there is no averment of the date of execution of " Will " and date of death of Testator, the father of the plaintiff and as such not admissible the basis of judgment of the courts below. He lastly submits that the findings of the trial court has not been controverted or reversed by the appellate court which is not sustainable in law and as such he prayed for to make the rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court.

8. In support of his contention he has referred the decisions reported in:(1) 38 DLR 39, (2) 39 DLR (AD) 46, (3)2 BLC 76, (4) 44 DLR 69.

9. Mr. Kazi Akter Hamid, the learned advocates appearing for the Opposite-parties who opposed the rule and submits that the plaintiff has rightly presented the " Will " before the Sub-registrar because section 40(1) which states "Otherwise under a will" and as such appellate court has rightly allowed the appeal. He submits that the moment the defendant Nos.4-6 came to know about the existence of " Will " they should have filed a separate suit for cancellation of registered deed of " Will " but they did not and as such they are estopped to deny under section 115 of the Evidence Act. He submits that the suit was filed in the year 1987 and still they did not file any written statement or any suit for cancellation of registered deed of " Will ". He further submits that section 117 of Mahomedan Law the words inserted there that inaction or silence cannot be basis of silence but no where it is said conduct cannot be basis of consent. He submits that the sisters had full consent and they were present in front of their father while he executed the deed of " Will " which is evident from evidence of P.W.2 Abdul Barek, husband of one of the sister, P.W.3 Abdul Hay, member and P.W.4 Nurul Huq Bepari. He submits that the sisters, defendant Nos.4-6 never contested the suit who were best witnesses under section 114 of the Evidence Act and testimonies of P.Ws.2,3 and 4 were not shaken. He lastly submits that the appellate court rightly discussed the evidence and reversed the finding of the trial court and reached in his decision and the decisions of the appellate court being last and final court of facts are not open to interference by this court in revision since there is no misreading and non-consideration of evidence.

10. In order to appreciate the submission made by the learned advocates for the parties, I have gone through the revisional application, pleadings, evidence, exhibits, judgment and decree of the courts below very carefully.

11. Now the question calls for consideration whether the learned Judge of the court of appeal below has committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree.

12. On perusal of the record it appears that the plaintiff brought the suit challenging the sale deed dated 14.7.1987 executed by the defendant Nos.4-6 in favour of defendant Nos. 1-4 claiming that defendant Nos.4-6 had no right, title to sale the suit land because the original owner of the land namely, lmanuddin father of plaintiff and defendant Nos. 4-6 had already executed " Will " in the year 1972 infavour of plaintiff which was registered on 14.5.1987 measuring 2.12 1/2 acres of land and the defendants transferred the same by a sale deed dated 14.7.1987.

13. The learned Judge of the trial court considering the evidence and materials on record dismissed the suit with the finding:

“আমরা পূর্বেই দেখিয়াছি প্রদর্শনী-১ অছিয়ত নামাটি ৪-২-১৯৭২ইং তারিখের ইমাম উদ্দিন কর্তৃক সম্পাদিত ও বিগত ১৪-৫-১৯৮৭ইং তারিখে বাদী কর্তৃক দীর্ঘ ১৫ বৎসর পর রেজিস্ট্রিকৃত। বাদীর বর্তমান বয়স ২৮ বৎসর তার মানে অছিয়ত টি সম্পাদনের সময় তাহার বয়স ছিল ১৩ বৎসর। অছিয়ত নামাটি কার্টিজ পেপারে লিখিত। উহা কি কারনে সুদীর্ঘ ১৫ বৎসর পর রেজিস্ট্রি হইল আরজীতে উহার কোন ব্যাখ্যা নাই। ইমাম উদ্দিন কবে মারা গেল, কবে অছিয়তটি বাদীর হস্তগত হইল বা কবে তিনি উহা সমন্ধে জানিত��� পারিলেন এই ব্যাপারে বাদী নীরব। ইমাম উদ্দিন জীবমানে কি কারনে অছিয়ত টি রেজিস্ট্রি করিয়া গেলেন না উহার ও কোন ব্যাখ্যা নাই। রেজিস্ট্রেশন আইনের নবম অধ্যায়ের বিধান মতে ইমাম উদ্দিনকে অছিয়ত টি রেজিস্ট্রারের নিকট জমা করিয়া রাখিতে ও দেখা যায় না। উপরোক্ত অবস্থায় পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে ইহা বলা যাইতে পারে যে, বাদী ৪-৬ নং বিবাদীগন কর্তৃক সম্পাদিত  ও ১-৩ নং বিবাদীগনের নালিশা দলিলটি ঠেকানের জন্য এবং তাহার ভগ্নী অর্থাৎ অংশীদারগনকে তাহাদের প্রাপ্য হিসাব হইতে বঞ্চিত করার কু-অভিপ্রায়ে প্রদর্শনী-১ অছিয়ত নামা দলিলটি সৃষ্টি করিয়াছে এবং উহাতে সম্পাদনের পূর্বের তারিখ দিয়াছে।”

14. The learned Judge of the appellate court considering the evidence and materials on record allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court with the finding:

“রেজিস্ট্রি আইনের ৪০(১) ও ৪১ ধারার বিধান মোতাবেক অছিয়ত নামাটি আইন সংগত ভাবে নিবন্ধিত হইয়াছে। অপরদিকে মুসলিম আইনের বিধান মোতাবেক অছিয়ত সম্পাদন কারীর অছিয়ত নামায় সম্পাদনের বিষয়ে কোন ওজর আপত্তি বিবাদী রেসপনডেন্ট এর নিকট হইতে না আসায় বাদী আপীলেন্টের দাবীকৃত প্রদ-১ অছিয়ত নামাটি আইন সংগত এবং বাদী আপীলেন্ট ব্যতিত অপরাপর ওয়ারিশগনের উক্ত অছিয়ত নামার বিষয়ে তাহাদের স্ব-স্ব কার্যাজনিত মানসিকতার প্রতিফলনের প্রেক্ষিতে উক্ত অছিয়ত নামায় ওয়ারিশগন সম্মতি রহিয়াছে ইতা সাক্ষ্য প্রমানে প্রতীয়মান হয় বিধায় অছিয়ত নামার ক তপছিলোক্তর ভূমির আন্তরে ২৪ শতাংশ ভূমি ১-৩ নং বিবাদী রেসপনডেন্টের বরাবরে বিগত ১৪/৭/১৯৮৭ইং তারিখের চিতোষী সাব-রেজিস্ট্রি অফিসের রেজিস্ট্রিকৃত ৪৬০২ নং সাব কবলা দলিলটি অকার্য্যকরী, বেআইনী বেদাড়া, তঞ্চকতা প্রবলের অযোগ্য এবং উহা বাদীর উপর বাধ্যকর নহে।

উপরোক্ত আলোচনার প্রেক্ষিতে অত্র আদালতের নিকট ইহা প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রদ-১ সম্পর্কিয় অছিয়ত নামাটির বিষয়ে রেজিষ্ট্রি সংক্রান্তে বিষয়ে যেমন ভুল সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করিয়াছেন, তেমনি উক্ত অছিয়ত নামার অপরাপর ওয়ারিশগন সম্পত্তি সংক্রান্ত আইনসংগত ব্যাখ্যা ঘটনা প্রবহের আলোকে সাক্ষ্য প্রমান মুল্যায়নে ব্যর্থ হইয়াছে। ফলে তর্কিত রায় ও ডিক্রীটি আইন সংগত হয় নাই। উহা রদ ও রহিত যোগ্য।”

<u>15. From a plain reading from above portion judgment of the appellate court it appears that the appellate court being last and final court of facts considering the evidence, materials on record and relevant provision of law has rightly allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment of the trial court.</u>

16. On perusal of the judgment of the appellate court it appears that the appellate court being last and final court of facts on assessing and re-assessing the evidence on record independently and reversed the findings of the trial court.

17. In the instant case the plaintiff presented the "Will" to the Sub-registrar Office for registration under section 40(1) as beneficiary otherwise under a "Will" may present it to any registrar or Sub-registrar for registration.

18. Section 27 of the Registration Act provides that "wills" may be presented or deposited for registration at any time.

<u>19. It appears that "Will" executed in the year 1972 and registered on 14.5.1987 whereas the defendant Nos.4-6 executed and registered a sale deed on 14.7.1987. The deed which executed earlier will prevail over the later on. In the instant case the "Will" was executed earlier than the deed of transfer and as such deed of "Will" will prevail over the deed of sale and registered 'Will' would remain in enforce unless the same was cancelled by an appropriate civil court.</u>

20. This view of mine find support in the case, (1) Rafiqul Islam (Md) Vs. Mir Abdul Ali, reported in 44 DLR(AD)176, wherein their lordships held:

"Sale deed executed earlier but registered later in point of time will prevail over sale deed executed later but registered earlier. The criterion in such cases ,for the purpose of determining when the sale takes effect is not the date of registration but the date of execution of the deed itself”

21. Mokbul Ahmed Mia alias Moqbul Ahmed and others Vs. Md. Golam Mostafa and another, reported in 12 BLC 177, wherein their lordships held:

"In the instant case it appears that the defendant No. 1 executed Jour kahalas on 21-4-1982 but the same wee registered on 18-8-1982 but defendants No.1 executed and registered kabala in favour of plaintiff on 23-4-1982, so, the kabalas which were executed on 21-4-1982 by the defendant No.1 in favour of defendant Nos. 2-5 shall prevail."

22. Abdul Mannan Bhuyan and others Vs. Md. Nasir Hossain and others, reported in 18 BLC(AD) 44, wherein their lordships held:

"S.A. and R.S. records were not an evidence of title and that a registered document would prevail upon the records of rights and that the registered document would remain in enforce unless the same was cancelled by an appropriate civil Court."

23. In view of the evidence and materials on record it appears to me that the findings arrived by the court of appeal below having been rested upon considerations and discussions of evidence and materials on record and also on a correct and proper analysis of the legal aspect involved in the case. The findings of the appellate court below are sound and sustainable in fact and law.

24. Moreover, the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate court below in its entirety are well founded in the facts and circumstances of the case. Therefore, grounds urged and the contentions advanced by the learned advocate for the petitioner are not correct exposition of law. However, 1 have gone through the decisions reported in :(1) 38 DLR 39, (2) 39 DLR (AD) 46, (3)2 BLC 76, (4) 44 DLR 69 referred by the learned advocate for the petitioner. I am respectful agreement with principles enunciated therein. But the facts leading to those cases are quite distinguishable to that of the instant case and therefore, to that effect I am also unable to accept his submissions. On the contrary the legal pleas taken by the learned advocate for Opposite party prevail and appear to have a good deal of force.

25. In view of discussion, decisions and reasons stated above, I am of the view that the impugned judgment and decree of the court of appeal below suffers from no legal infirmity which calls for no interference by this court in revision. Thus, the rule has no merit.

26. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The judgment and decree of the Appellate court in Title Appeal No.51 of 1991 is hereby affirmed. There will be no order as to costs.

27. The order of stay granted earlier by this court stands vacated.

28. Let the Lower Court Records along with a copy of the judgment be sent at once.

End.

Shoukat Ali Khan with Salma Masud Chowdhury, Advocates— For the Plaintiff
