full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why judgment and decree dated 16-3-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna, in Title Appeal No. 121 of 2000 allowing the appeal in part by way of modifying the judgment and decree dated 13-3-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Khulna, in Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 dismissing the suit, should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that opposite party No. 1 herein as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 in the 3rd Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Khulna, for declaration of Title in respect of 0.471/3 acres land out of 1.43 acres as 1/3rd share by way of inheritance described in schedule "Ka" of the plaint and for further declaration that the deed of gift No. 3315 dated 14-12-1997 registered at Batiagata Sub registry office is forged, fraudulent, inoperative, void and not binding upon the plaintiff.

3. Plaintiffs case in short is that suit land belonged to Bhabesh Mondol who married Purnima Rani, daughter of Pulin Bairagee. Out of the wedlock, plaintiff was born who was brought up in the house of his maternal uncle. Since Purnima lost her procreation capacity, Bhabesh Mondol married Renuka and out of that wedlock two sons namely, Bhudeb and Bidhu were born. In the year 1997, Bhabesh was admitted in Khulna Seba Clinic for treatment. Bhabesh was a heart patient. At critical stage of his ailment, Bhabesh was again admitted at Batiagata Health Complex and remained there till 18-12-1997. Plaintiff was residing at Chittagong for the purpose of his service. His mother was at his maternal uncle's house. Bhudeb, Bidhu and their mother Renuka looked after Bhabesh at the clinic. Taking advantage of the situation, on 14-12-1997 defendant No. 1 and her two sons took Bhabesh out of the clinic for 2 (two) hours by executing a bond and within this time in collusion with the sub registrar created a forged deed of gift dated 14-12-1997 in respect of the suit land. Said deed of gift was not executed voluntarily by Bhabesh. Bhabesh died on 19-4-1998 without any treatment. After the cremation ceremony, defendant No. 1 disclosed about the deed of gift. Then the plaintiff procured certified copy of the deed on 17-5-1998 and constrained to file the suit.

4. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and contending inter alia that there is no cause of action, suit is not maintainable, bad for defect of parties and barred by limitation. Further contending that Bhabesh Mondol willingly and voluntarily executed and registered the deed of gift in favour of his wife. She is in possession of the land. Plaintiff is not son of Bhabesh Mondol. All the rituals after expiry of Bhabesh Mondol were performed by the defendant and her two sons. Suit is liable to be dismissed.

5. After hearing the parties and assessing evidenced on record, .learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit on contest against defendant No. 1 and exparte against the rest holding that plaintiff did not pray for cancellation of the deed and the suit is bad for defect of parties and also held that suit for declaration on an undemarcated and unspecified land is not maintainable.

6. Being aggrieved, plaintiff as appellant filed Title Appeal No. 121 of 2000 in the Court of learned District Judge, Khulna. On transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna, who after hearing the parties and reassessing evidence on record allowed the appeal in part upholding portion of the judgment and decree passed by the trial court so far as it relates to declaration of title but decreed that the deed of gift dated 14-12-1997 is forged, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff.

7. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree, defendant-respondent as petitioner preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present rule with an order of stay.

8. Mr. Zainul Abedin with Mr M Mahbubur Rahman, learned advocates appearing for the petitioner submits that appellate court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree without adverting findings of the trial court and thus violated provisions of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure as such, impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He also submits that appellate court below committed an illegality in not considering that plaintiff filed the suit praying for declaration that the deed of gift dated 14-12-1997 is forged and fraudulent as such, burden of proof lies upon the plaintiff under section 103 of the Evidence Act to prove that the registered deed of gift is executed and registered fraudulently. He next submits that since the deed of gift is duly registered it has presumption of genuineness and correctness under section 114(e) of the Evidence Act and the appellate court below committed an illegality without considering this legal aspect. He again submits that appellate court below allowed the appeal with extraneous finding that the deed of gift was not acted upon without looking into the provisions of section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act inasmuch as amongst Hindus gift make subsequent to the Act does not require delivery of possession if there is registration. He lastly submits that the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court below is based on misreading and non appreciation of evidence on record and as such liable to be set aside. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Abani Mohan Saha vs Assistant Custodian (SDO) Vested Property, Chandpur, reported in 39 DLR (AD) 323 and the case of Abul Kashem Howlader vs Sultan Ahmed, reported in 9 BLC 333.

9. On the other hand, Mr. Anwarul Islam Shahin with Ms Farjana Sharmin, learned advocates for the opposite party submits that since the defendant No. 1 claims title in the suit land by dint of deed of gift dated 14-12-1997, duty cast upon her under the provisions of sections 101 and 103 of the Evidence Act to prove that the deed was acted upon. He also submits that it is apparent from evidence on record that at the time of execution and registration of the deed of gift, the donor was critically ill and admitted in the hospital so, it can be easily presumed that the deed of gift was not executed and registered voluntarily. He next submits that from the circumstances which is proved by the witnesses, it is evident that at the time of execution and registration of the deed of gift, the donor was not physically and mentally sound and the same is also proved from the testimony of PW 5 i.e. doctor of the clinic. He next submits that the very circumstances of the clinic wherein plaintiff and his mother were absent proves that the deed of gift executed under undue influence by defendant No. 1 and her two sons to deprive the plaintiff from his due share. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Official Assignee of Bengal vs Bidyasundari Dasi, reported in 24 CWN 145.

10. Heard the learned advocates. Perused revisional application, judgment of the courts below along with lower courts record and the decisions cited by the learned advocates.

11. Admittedly plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration of title in respect of "Ka" schedule land and for further declaration that the deed of gift dated 14-12-1997 registered at Batiagata sub register office is forged, fraudulent void inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff. Deed of gift dated 14-12-1997 which is under challenge is a registered instrument. It is not a case of the plaintiff that said deed was not executed and registered by Bhabesh Mondol rather plaintiff case is that the donor did not execute and register the deed voluntarily and willingly but under undue influence of defendant No. 1 and her sons.

<u>12. I have gone through the judgments passed by the trial court as well as appellate court below. Plaintiff filed the suit under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. By now it is settled that a suit for mere declaration without seeking cancellation of the document is not maintainable. Further that the impugned deed of gift which is duly registered has a presumption of correctness as provided under section 114 (e) of the Evidence Act as such onus lies upon the plaintiff to prove that the deed is forged and fabricated. On perusal of the record, it is evident that plaintiff failed to prove that the deed of gift is forged and fabricated by adducing credible oral and documentary evidence. From deposition of PW 5, it appears that the donor was permitted by the doctor to go out of the clinic for two hours, when the deed was executed and registered. Appellate court below allowed the appeal in part holding that the deed was not acted upon since there is no evidence that possession was delivered to the defendant No. 1. This finding is not correct. Where the instrument of gift has been registered, delivery of possession is not essential for the validity of a gift by a Hindu.</u>

13. Section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act runs as follows:

"123. Transfer how effected—For the purpose of making a gift of immovable property, the transfer must be effected by a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the donor, and attested by at least two witnesses.

[Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, a heba under Muhammadan law shall be deemed to be a gift of immovable property for the aforesaid purpose.]

For the purpose of making a gift of movable property, the transfer may be affected either by registered instrument signed as aforesaid or by delivery.

Such delivery may be made in the same way as goods sold may be delivered."

14. On plain reading of section 123, it is clear that delivery of possession is essential to the validity of a gift is abrogated by section 123 of the Act. A gift under the Act can only be affected in a manner provided by section 123.

15. On perusal of the testimony of DWs it appears that DW 4 is an attesting witness of the deed of gift and DW 5 is scribe of the deed but the appellate court below on the basis of testimony of DWs 2 and 3 arrived at a finding that DWs 2-4 did not hear about the deed of gift when Bhabesh was alive. But on perusal of the testimony of DWs 2, 3 and 4, it is apparent that the appellate court below arrived at such a finding on misreading of evidence. In such view of the matter, I am of the opinion that the appellate court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree.

16. Facts and circumstances of the case cited by the learned advocate for the opposite party is quite distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the case in hand.

17. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

18. Judgment and decree dated 16-3-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna, in Title Appeal No. 121 of 2000 is set aside and the judgment and decree dated 13-3-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Khulna, in Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 is hereby restored.

19. Order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the rule is vacated.

Send down lower courts record along with a copy of this judgment to the court concern at once.

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the Opposite Party No. 1, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 25-7-2018, passed by the Election Appellate Tribunal, Jamalpur, in Election Appeal No.5 of 2017, dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 23-8-2017, passed by the Election Tribunal, Jamalpur, in Election Case No.30 of 2016, allowing the election petition should not be set-aside and/or such other order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper should not be passed.

2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that, the opposite party No.1, Zobed Ali, as petitioner, had filed Election Case No.30 of 2016 before the Election Tribunal (the ET), comprised of the Senior Assistant Judge, Jamalpur, alleging inter-alia that, while the ballot papers were being sorted out, at least 200 ballots were removed from the pile of the petitioner bearing his election symbol "cock" and were with ballot papers bearing the symbol "football" of his rival candidate Md Alam Miah, while another 47 number of ballots were cancelled unlawfully by the Presiding Officer. In this way, the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 had managed to show Md Alam Miah (contested with the symbol "football") as the elected member, in that election, by a margin of 30 votes. Further allegations of the petitioner are that, the agent of Zobed Ali was forcefully ousted from the polling booth and the petitioner, then and there, had verbally raised objection to the Presiding Officer (PO), but the PO did not pay any heed to it, rather the PO with the help of law enforcing agencies, shifted the ballot papers from the polling booth to another place and had declared Md Alam Miah elected by a margin of 30 votes. He also alleged that, the activities of the PO were illegal, the result declared was also illegal and if the ballot papers are recounted, the actual poll result will come out in favour of the election-petitioner i.e. the present opposite party No.1, Zobed Ali. Accordingly, by filing an election petition before the ET, he has prayed for recounting the ballot papers of the concerned Union Parishad election in which he has contested as a candidate for the post of an Union Parishad Member.

3. The present petitioner, as OP No. 1 in the E.T. case, had contested before the ET, by filing a written objection, denying all material allegations made in the petition.

4. The petitioner has examined 4 witnesses to support his case and the opposite party No. 1 has also examined himself as DW 1.

5. The ET after hearing the parties and having assessed the evidence on record, allowed the election petition and passed an order, on 23-8-2017, for recounting the ballot papers alongwith the counter foils.

6. Against the said judgment and order of the ET, the present petitioner, preferred Election Appeal No.5 of 2017 (as appellant) before the two members Election Appellate Tribunal (EAT) comprising of the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Jamalpur, and the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Jamalpur, that has passed the impugned judgment and order dated 25-7-2018, dismissing the appeal and thereby, affirming the judgment and order dated 23-8-2017 of the ET.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the EAT, the petitioner has filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

8. Mr Md Shahabul Alam Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent-petitioner submits that, the result of the election was published in the gazette notification on 23-6-2016, but the election petition was filed on 24-7-2017 i.e. after expiry of the stipulated period of 30 days. Hence, this petition is barred by limitation as per the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 23 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Act, 2009. He next submits that, sub-section 2(Ka) of section 39 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Act, 2009 provides for recounting the ballot papers by the PO on the basis of written objection of an aggrieved candidate, but the election petitioner did not file any such application to the PO (Presiding Officer) praying for recounting the ballot papers. Hence, the petition filed under section 22 of the said Act was not proper and it was prematured one. Therefore, this petition is also not maintainable, but the ET as well as the EAT had failed to appreciate this law point, while passing the impugned judgment and order. He has, next, drawn my attention to the deposition of the PWs and the DW and further submits that, there is no adequate proof to support the allegations of the election-petitioner, who is the present opposite party No. 1 in this revisional application. He continues that, one Sultan, polling agent of the election-petitioner, has signed the result sheet, that records that Md Alam Miah has been declared elected, but the ET, as well as the EAT both have failed to take into notice this aspect of the case and have arrived at wrong findings, whereupon they have passed the impugned judgment and orders dismissing the appeal and thereby the EAT has committed error of law, resulting in error in the decision and that has failure of justice. The learned Advocate has prayed for making the Rule absolute by setting aside the concurrent findings of the courts below. The learned Advocate for the revision-petitioner has cited certain decision in support of their case, which will be discussed at the relevant place hereinafter.

9. On the other hand, Mr Md Mahbubur Rashid, appeared on behalf of the Opposite party No. 1. The learned Advocate submits that the petition filed under section 22 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ain, 2009 is not barred by limitation. He also submits that this revisional application filed under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, by the petitioner, is not maintainable in as much as sub-section (6) of section 23 of the said Act clearly stipulates that, the decision of the Election Appellate Tribunal shall be final. Therefore, this revisional application is liable to be rejected on this ground alone. He next submits that, the evidence placed before the tribunal is adequate and the aggrieved party i.e. Zobed Ali has proved the allegations, made in the election petition, by adducing sufficient evidence before the tribunal. Besides, the testimony of the deponents are consistent and that none of them could be discredited, as regards the case of the election-petitioner, during his cross examination. He proceeds on that, although the present petitioner referred to "Form Neo (2)", at the time of argument before the High Court Division, however, he did not file this form before the tribunal only to suppress the fact of rigging in the election. Therefore, the submissions based on Form Neo (2) are totally baseless, inadmissible and irrelevant. He then submits that, there is no merit in this Rule. Hence, he has prayed for discharging the Rule.

10. I have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties, perused the application for revision, lower Court's record as well as the judgment of both the Courts below and other materials on record and also the cited decisions.

11. First of all I should consider as to whether the petition is barred by limitation or not. Sub-section (2) of section 23 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Act, 2009, reads as follows:

“ (২) কোন সংক্ষুব্ধ ব্যক্তি ত্রিশ নির্বাচিত চেয়ারম্যান বা সদস্য বা সদস্যগণের নাম সরকারি গেজেটে প্রকাশের পরবর্তী ৩০(ত্রিশ) দিনের মধ্যে নির্বাচনী দরখাস্ত দায়ের করিতে পারিবেন।

12. A mere perusal of the provisions quoted above will show that, the period of 30 days shall be counted from the date next to the date on which the gazette has been published. In other words, in counting the 30 days period, for the purpose of sub-section (2) of section 23, quoted above, the day on which the gazette notification has been published shall be excluded.

13. In this case, gazette notification has been published on 23-6-2016. Therefore, the 30 days period shall be counted from 24-6-2016. Accordingly, I hold that the period of 30 days shall expire on 23-7-2016, in this case. The month of June is of 30 days. But, 23-7-2016 being Saturday or weekly holyday, therefore, it has been filed on the next working day, which is permissible and valid as per provisions of section 10 of the General Closes Act, 1897. Therefore, the election petition has been filed within the stipulated period of time.

14. Next, I find that sub-rule (2) of Rule 39 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Election Rule, 2010 stipulates that,

৩৯ ভোট গণনাঃ ৩৯২) প্রিজাইডিং অফিসার নিম্নলিখিত ক্ষেত্রে পুনরায় ভোট গণনা করিতে পারিবেন, যথাঃ

“(ক) প্রয়োজনে, স্বীয় উদ্যোগে, বা (খ) কোন প্রতিদ্বন্থী প্রার্থীর বা নির্বাচনী এজেন্টের বা পোলিং এজেন্টের সুনির্দিষ্ট লিখিত আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে, যদি তাহার নিকট আবেদনটি যুক্তিযুক্ত বলিয়া নির্বাচিত হয়।

15. A mere perusal of sub-rule (2) of Rule 39 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Election Rule, 2010, clearly shows that, this is simply an enabling provision and this is not a precondition for filing a petition under section 22 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Act, 2009. Besides, the Presiding Officer, under that Act, does not have the power or jurisdiction similar to that of or as can be exercised by the Election Tribunal. In that sense, the Presiding Officer does not enjoy any concurrent jurisdiction with the Election Tribunal. On the other hand, here the Presiding Officer is the opposite party No. 2 in the election petition.

16. The jurisdiction conferred under sections 22 and 23 of the Act is specified and exclusive one in which the Presiding Officer or the Returning Officer themselves could be the opposite parties or the accuseds. The law would have made no sense if it were mandatory that any objection should, first of all, be made to the Presiding Officer. Hence, I find no substances in the submission made referring to Rule 39(2).

17. It is, therefore, clear that section 22 and 23 of the Act confers a special statutory and exclusive jurisdiction in the election tribunal, and exercise of such jurisdiction does not depend on filing a prior application, for recounting the ballots, before the Presiding Officer, who, himself, might also be a party to an election dispute to be resolved by the ET.

18. Besides, from the deposition of the witnesses given before the election tribunal (ET), it is clear that, immediately after the incident took place, complainant had made verbal objection to the Presiding Officer, but the Presiding Officer did not pay any heed to his objection, rather with the help of the law enforcing agencies, the PO had shifted the ballots from the polling booth and had counted the ballot papers behind the back of the election-petitioner or his agent. I do not find any situation in the record that could have justified such conduct of the Presiding Officer, which is apparently unfair and unwarranted. No law and order situation of that degree had arisen to justify shifting the ballots to other places and then counting them .behind the back of the election-petitioner and to declare the result behind his back.

19. The submission that the agent of the election-petitioner has signed a "Form Neo (2)," as per Rule 39 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Rules, I find that no such document has been placed or proved, before the Election Tribunal, by the present-petitioner or the 2 or 3, who are respectively the rival candidate, the Presiding Officer and the Returning Officer. Hence, I would not take into consideration the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, made on this point, rather I would draw a presumption, as per section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, 1872, that if Form Neo (2) were placed before the Election Tribunal, then the case would have gone against the original opposite party No. 1 (the present petitioner). Therefore, they have suppressed the actual fact in not filing the said Form Neo (2).

<u>20. I, however, appreciate the submission and professionalism of the learned Advocate for the petitioner who has cited the decision reported in BLD 1986 (AD) 236, in a case between Md Shajahan vs Md Sadeq = 38 DLR (AD) 275; wherein it has been observed by the Appellate Division that, "Ballot papers have special sanctity of their own and their secrecy should not be infringed by reopening the Scaled packets, unless the recounting becomes indispensably necessary to determine the dispute. When recounting would become so necessary depends on circumstances in each case".</u>

<u>21. The decision reported in BLD 1986 (AD) 236 = 38 DLR (AD) 275; provides a complete guide line as regards the case for recounting of the ballot and when it should be allowed. In the fact and circumstances of this case, I am of the opinion that, in this case, the election has been materially affected by the illegal acts alleged in this election petition and duly proved before the Election Tribunal.</u>

22. I find no illegality or irregularity or any misinterpretation of law or of facts in passing the impugned judgment and order.

23. However, before parting off I must turn my attention to sub-section (6) of section 23 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ain, 2009 which runs as follows:

“(৬) নির্বাচনী আপিল ট্রাইব্যুনালের রায় চুড়ান্ত বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে।

<u>24. Therefore, in view of the attribute of `finality' of the judgment and order of the Election Appellate Tribunal, as imposed by section 23(6) of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Act, 2009, this Rule is liable to be discharged for want of statutory jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, without further discussion. However, such finality clause does not take away or oust the constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court Division, vested in it under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in as much as, the Judicial Power of the State vests in the Supreme Court, which cannot be curtailed or abrogated or abridged by an Act of Parliament.</u>

25. Be that as it may, I have touched the merit as well to prevent any chance of agitating the self-same matter before the Writ Bench, for further lingering of this matter in another forum, while nearly 4 (four) years have gone out of 5 (five) years term.

26. This is a clear case for awarding cost of Taka 1,00,000, but considering the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and for taking lenient view, I refrain from awarding cost.

27. I do not find any merit in this Rule.

28. In the result, the Rule is discharged.

29. The impugned judgment and order dated 25-7-2018, passed by the learned the Judge of the Election Appellate Tribunal, Jamalpur in Election Appeal No.5 of 2017, dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 23-8-2017, passed by the Judge of the Election Tribunal, Jamalpur, in Election Case No.30 of 2016 allowing, is hereby upheld.

30. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

31. I record appreciation of the co-operation rendered to this Court, in the disposal of this matter, by the learned Advocates for both sides.

32. No costs.

Let a copy of this judgment along with the Lower Court's Record be sent down to the concerned Courts at once.
